title: The Frozen Period requires an Atlas Edit Proposal to sit unchanged before it can be formally submitted
content:
A.1.12.2.1.4 defines the review stage of the Monthly Cycle with two separate clocks. The **Feedback Period** is "the minimum amount of time within which the community can give feedback in response to an Atlas Edit Proposal before it can advance to Formal Submission." The **Frozen Period** is "the minimum amount of time during which an Atlas Edit Proposal must remain unchanged before it can advance to Formal Submission." The Atlas notes "These periods can overlap."

The Frozen Period is the non-obvious half, and it closes a loophole the Feedback Period alone leaves open. A proposal could satisfy any consultation requirement and then be materially rewritten just before submission — collecting the legitimacy of a review process that examined different text. Freezing the document decouples *time available to review* from *time the reviewed object has existed*, so what voters see is what was actually scrutinized.

Allowing the two periods to overlap is a deliberate efficiency: feedback and stability are not sequential requirements, so a proposal that draws comment without needing revision advances at the pace of the longer clock rather than their sum. The implicit penalty falls on late redrafting — every substantive edit restarts the freeze and pushes the proposal toward the next Formal Submission Window, which A.1.12.2.1.6 confines to two days starting 00:00 UTC on the first Monday of the cycle.
description: Two minimum durations govern review — a Feedback Period for community input and a Frozen Period of textual stability — and they are allowed to overlap.
